title: datetime.now() without a timezone produces a naive datetime that cannot be compared to an aware datetime.

root_cause.title: datetime.now() without a timezone produces a naive datetime that cannot be compared to an aware datetime.
root_cause.pattern: datetime.now() called without timezone argument when the other operand is an aware datetime, causing a TypeError at comparison or arithmetic.

twins.reasoning: renews_at is documented as timezone-aware; datetime.now() is naive, so both the comparison on line 17 and the subtraction on line 23 raise TypeError under the same conditions as the original bug.
valid_until is documented as timezone-aware; datetime.now() on lines 17 and 23 is naive, identical mistake with reversed operand order on line 17.
expires_at and created_at are documented as timezone-aware; datetime.now() on lines 17 and 23 is naive, same comparison and arithmetic mistake.

variants.description: Reversed operands: datetime.now() > deadline instead of deadline < datetime.now(timezone.utc)
datetime.utcnow() used instead of datetime.now() — also naive, same TypeError with aware operand
Naive datetime.now() result stored in a local variable 'now' before the comparison
Same mistake introduced in a brand-new module src/reminders.py
datetime.utcnow() used in arithmetic subtraction (sessions.py session_age_seconds)
Naive datetime.now() wrapped in a private helper _get_now() then called in arithmetic
